senses.gloss:
ध्मा 1. ध्मा, cl. 1. P. धमति, दध्मौ,
ध्मास्यति (ep. धमिष्यति), अध्मासीत्,
ध्मातुम्, to blow (as wind or breath), breathe out,
exhale; to blow (a conch-shell, trumpet, or any wind
instrument), to produce sound by blowing; to blow
a fire, excite fire by blowing; to excite sparks; to
manufacture by blowing, melt, smelt; to blow away
from one's self, cast, throw: Pass. ध्मायते, ep.
and Ved. धम्यते, ध्मायति, to be blown, to be
melted, &c.: Caus. ध्मापयति, &c., to cause to
blow or melt, to consume by fire, burn: Desid.
दिध्मासति: Intens. देध्मीयते, दाध्माति (दा-
ध्मायते), to be blown violently; [cf. Lat. flā-
re; Old Germ. blayan, blāhan, blāsan, ‘blow;’
Gr. σμώ-νη, σμώ-ς ?].

2. ध्मा, आस्, m. (?), blowing.
—ध्मा-कार, अस्,
m. a blacksmith, a smith.

ध्म, अस्, आ, अम्, blowing; [cf. तूणव-ध्˚ and
शङ्ख-ध्˚.]

ध्मात, अस्, आ, अम्, blown (as a wind instru-
ment), blown into, blown up, inflated, blown by a
bellows (a fire &c.), inflamed, puffed, excited.

ध्मातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be blown, to be ex-
cited or kindled.
ध्मान, अम्, n. blowing, puffing, swelling.

ध्मापित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), reduced to
ashes, burnt to cinder.

ध्मायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, or ध्मायमान, अस्, आ,
अम्, being blown; being melted, &c.

ध्माङ्क्ष् ध्माङ्क्ष् (various reading for
ध्वाङ्क्ष्), cl. 1. P. ध्माङ्क्षति,
&c., to crow or caw; to desire; [cf. ध्राक्ष्.]

ध्माङ्क्ष, अस्, m. a crow, &c.; (wrong form
for ध्वाङ्क्ष, q. v.)

ध्मामन् ध्मामन्, आ, m. wrong reading for
ध्यामन्, col. 2.
